workshop.subtitle: Agentic AI for Extended Reality
workshop.fullName: The 1st International Workshop on Agentic AI for Extended Reality

hero.eyebrow: Co-located with IEEE ISMAR 2026 — Bari, Italy — Tuesday 6 October 2026, Morning Session
hero.blurb: XRAG '26 is a focused venue for researchers, designers, practitioners, and industry experts exploring how AI agents can perceive, reason, remember, plan, and act in XR systems while keeping people in control.

about.title: XR is entering a new phase: situated, controllable, human-centered Agentic AI.
about.areasTitle: The five research macro-areas of XRAG '26
about.areasIntro: XRAG '26 is organized around five interconnected research macro-areas. They frame the call for papers, structure the workshop discussion, and define the scope of contributions we welcome.
paragraphs: Immersive systems are no longer limited to visualization, spatial interaction, or situated perception, while AI assistants are moving beyond chat-based interfaces toward multimodal, tool-using, and context-aware systems. Advances in foundation models, egocentric perception, wearable sensing, generative AI, memory, and autonomous planning are creating the conditions for a new class of agentic XR systems.

These systems can perceive physical and virtual environments, reason over spatial and multimodal context, remember user goals and environmental states, act through digital or embodied tools, and return control to users through immersive, wearable, and spatial interfaces.

XRAG '26 brings together XR, Agentic AI, Human-Computer Interaction, Cognitive Science, and applied research communities around one concrete question: how should we design, evaluate, and govern XR systems in which AI agents can perceive, reason, remember, plan, and act?

pillars.title: Agentic Architectures and Spatial Intelligence for XR
pillars.text: AI agents for AR/MR/VR, spatial computing, perception–reasoning–planning–action pipelines, and multimodal foundation models in immersive systems.

pillars.title: Egocentric, Multimodal, and Wearable AI Agents
pillars.text: Smart-glasses assistants, egocentric vision, multimodal sensing, and real-time situated perception across physical, virtual, and mixed environments.

pillars.title: Immersive Human-Agent Interaction, Control, and Collaboration
pillars.text: Human–agent collaboration, delegation, interruption and recovery, spatial feedback, trust, and human-centered interaction design.

pillars.title: Memory, Personalization, Tool Use, and Creative XR Workflows
pillars.text: Long-term memory, personalization, tool-using agents, AI-assisted XR authoring, generative 3D content, and iterative creative workflows.

pillars.title: Applications, Deployment, and Societal Impact of Agentic XR
pillars.text: Real-world agentic XR in industry, education, healthcare, cultural heritage, and entertainment, with attention to privacy, safety, accessibility, and governance.

topics.lead: A range of topics, which embrace different disciplines and perspectives, are invited to contribute to XRAG '26, including, but not restricted to:
items: Agentic architectures for AR, MR, and VR systems
AI agents for spatial computing and immersive environments
Wearable AI assistants and smart-glasses-based agents
Multimodal foundation models for XR interaction
Tool-using agents in immersive and spatial interfaces
Long-term memory, context modeling, and personalization in XR agents
Human-agent collaboration and human-AI teaming in AR/MR/VR
Proactive, context-aware, and adaptive XR agents
Spatial feedback, explanations, and legibility of agent actions
Human control, delegation, interruption, and recovery mechanisms
AI-assisted XR authoring and content generation
Agentic AI for creativity, co-creation, and creative workflows in XR
Generative 3D content, scene understanding, and world modeling
Evaluation methods, metrics, and benchmarks for agentic XR systems
Trust, safety, reliability, privacy, accessibility, ethics, and governance of agentic XR
Applications in education, healthcare, cultural heritage, industry, creativity, entertainment, and everyday computing
Position papers on future research agendas for agentic AI and XR

callForPapers.lead: XRAG '26 seeks several types of contributions at the intersection of Agentic AI and Extended Reality, including:

categories.title: Full research papers
categories.text: up to 6 pages (including references); mature research contributions, system papers, evaluations, datasets, methods, or theoretical frameworks.

categories.title: Short / work-in-progress papers
categories.text: up to 4 pages (including references); early-stage research, preliminary results, technical explorations, prototype descriptions, or emerging ideas.

categories.title: Position papers
categories.text: 2–4 pages (including references); critical perspectives, conceptual arguments, design principles, or taxonomies.

categories.title: Demo papers
categories.text: 2–4 pages (including references); demonstrations of working prototypes, interactive systems, XR applications, agentic interfaces, authoring tools, datasets, or technical showcases.

callForPapers.review: All submissions are peer-reviewed by the workshop organizers and program committee. Each paper receives at least two reviews. Criteria: relevance to agentic XR, originality, clarity, methodological soundness, technical feasibility, and potential to stimulate discussion.
callForPapers.publication: Each accepted workshop paper is included in the ISMAR 2026 Adjunct proceedings and IEEE Xplore, subject to the final ISMAR workshop publication policy, registration requirements, and camera-ready guidelines.

talk.title: AI and XR: how the knowledge is used for customisation
abstract: In the era of Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Worlds capable of almost anything, can we truly consider the knowledge embedded in digital tools a driver for personalizing products and services? Can these technologies become pivotal in fostering inclusion and enhancing human well-being?

In a landscape defined by increasingly rapid technological, economic, and social transformations, adaptability has emerged as a strategic competency — not only for individuals but also for the tools they use.

This keynote explores how digital environments — and virtual environments in particular — can be personalized to suit the context, the task, and the user (including their specific needs) through the use of knowledge-based AI. Drawing on real-world examples from the manufacturing and healthcare sectors, as well as field experiences and insights, the presentation aims to outline a potential path for future development.
A brief overview of national and European initiatives will round out the picture of the possibilities that AI and XR can offer.

bio: Dr. Marco Sacco, Research Director, Head of the CNR-STIIMA branch office in Lecco (''Human-Centered Living Environment''). Vice President of EuroXR (European Association for XR Technologies) with responsibility for European Union issues and collaborations. EuroXR is the oldest European association on XR technologies (funded in 2010) and the annual conference is at its 23rd edition.

Member of the Board of the VWA (Virtual World Association) representing the National Council of Italy. The association has entered into a partnership with the European Commission to improve and promote immersive technologies, extended reality, digital twins, virtual collaborative spaces, interoperability, and digital skills.
His experience (since 1994) concerns XR technologies (VR/MR/AR) and AI applied to both the manufacturinge and the health and well-being sectors.
Cluster Manager for the TechforLife Foundation (Lombardy Region Technology Cluster for Living Environment Technologies).

He has coordinated European (two of the largest EU projects under the 6th and 7th Framework Programmes) and national/regional projects. He has served as an expert on several R&D project evaluation committees, both at the European and national/regional levels.
He has authored over 180 publications, including articles in academic journals and conference proceedings.
